learning_objective: 🎯 Unlock the secrets of heredity! Understand how traits are passed from parents to offspring and the mathematical laws that govern genetics.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Traits are controlled by discrete units called factors (genes). In a dissimilar pair of factors (heterozygous like Tt), one dominates (Tall) and the other is recessive (dwarf).
During gamete formation (meiosis), the alleles for a trait separate, so each gamete receives only one allele. A parent with 'Tt' makes 'T' sperm/eggs and 't' sperm/eggs.
When studying two pairs of traits (like seed color and seed shape), the inheritance of one trait is completely independent of the inheritance of the other trait.
Exceptions to Mendel! Incomplete dominance: Red flower + White flower = Pink flower (blending). Codominance: Blood type A + Blood type B = Blood type AB (both expressed equally).

Discovered by Morgan in fruit flies. Genes located very close to each other on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together (Linkage), defying Independent Assortment. Recombination separates them.

fun_activity.title: 🎲 The Punnett Coin Flip
fun_activity.instructions: Take two coins. Heads = Dominant allele (Brown eyes), Tails = Recessive (Blue eyes). Flip both. HH or HT = Brown eyes. TT = Blue eyes. You just did a genetic cross!

exam_tips: 📌 Always memorize the standard phenotypic ratios: Monohybrid cross is 3:1. Dihybrid cross is 9:3:3:1.
📌 A 'Test Cross' is when you cross an organism with a dominant phenotype with a homozygous recessive organism to find out if it is homozygous or heterozygous.
📌 Know the difference: 'Genotype' is the letters (TT, Tt), 'Phenotype' is what you actually see (Tall, Short).
quick_recap: ⭐ Gregor Mendel is the Father of Genetics. He used pea plants because they have easily observable, contrasting traits.
⭐ The Chromosomal Theory of Inheritance (Sutton & Boveri) states that chromosomes are the physical carriers of Mendel's genes.
⭐ Human sex is determined by the XY system (XX is female, XY is male), where the male gamete determines the sex of the child.
